header: House prep recipes for bitters, foams, creams, a soda and food preps
(after 20261018030000). Stage 4F of the bottle catalog plan:
https://claude.ai/artifact/Vu6seuSNtN42nKYb2nDCVR
* 20 shared catalog preps that had no recipe get one, each from the pages
it cites (one item_sources row per recipe, yield and keep fact; two
sites for the staples): house aromatic bitters, siphon foams and
creams (coconut, egg white, strawberry, orange, ube, whipped cream,
pandan cream), sobolo, herb oils, lemon curd, miso caramel, quick
pickles, dashi, leche de tigre, lacto-fermented tomato and chilli, and
Swiss meringue.
* Keeps for herb oils, dairy, eggs, pickles and curd come from food
safety pages (NCHFP, Ohio State and other extension services) where
they are shorter than the recipe's own. Dill oil applies a general soft
herb ratio and says it's a starting point.
* Held back: House tonic (no source shows its quinine under the US 83 ppm
or FSANZ 100 mg/kg limits) and Cola syrup (its only source, the
OpenCola formula, is GPL-licensed).
* New plain ingredients: Cream charger, Grapeseed oil, Groundnut oil,
Pickling salt and Red miso; Malt powder too where a database lacks it
(production has it).
* An independent second check of every fact in this stage (102) against
the cited pages found none wrong.

ingredients.name: Cream charger
ingredients.description: An 8 g steel cartridge of nitrous oxide (N2O) that charges a cream siphon to whip cream and make foams. One charges a 0.5 L siphon.

ingredients.name: Grapeseed oil
ingredients.description: A light, neutral oil pressed from grape seeds. It stays liquid in the fridge, which makes it a good base for herb oils.

ingredients.name: Groundnut oil
ingredients.description: Peanut oil: a neutral cooking oil with a mild flavour. Made from peanuts, so flag it for allergies.

ingredients.name: Malt powder
ingredients.description: Powdered malted barley, sold as malted milk powder or plain malt powder. Adds a toasty, biscuity sweetness to creams and shakes.

ingredients.name: Pickling salt
ingredients.description: Fine pure salt with no iodine or anti-caking agents, sold for canning and pickling so brines stay clear.

ingredients.name: Red miso
ingredients.description: Aka miso: a longer-aged soybean paste, darker, saltier and more savoury than white miso.

preps.name: Basil oil
preps.description: A bright green oil made by blanching basil and blending it with grapeseed oil, then dripping it clear. For drops on foamy or savoury drinks and garnishes.

keeps.storage: Fridge at 4 °C or below, sealed bottle

steps.body: Blanch the basil in salted boiling water for 10 seconds, then straight into iced water. Drain and pat it very dry.
Blend the basil with the oil in a tall, narrow container until smooth.
Drip through paper towel or a double layer of cheesecloth for 5 hours, or overnight in the fridge. Don't press. Discard the solids.
Botulism risk: fresh herbs in oil must stay cold. Bottle, refrigerate straight away, label with the date, and throw it out after 4 days (or freeze it).

sources.note: Ricardo: 2 cups (70 g) basil leaves and stems to 1 1/2 cups (375 ml) grapeseed oil, blanched 10 seconds, strained 5 hours or overnight. Used as written.
Great British Chefs' general herb oil (basil named) runs heavier on herbs: 200 g herbs to 300 g oil. We use Ricardo's basil-specific ratio.
About 1 1/4 cups (310 ml).
NCHFP's rule for fresh garlic in oil, from its research on vegetables and herbs stored in oil: fridge at 4 °C or below, no more than 4 days, or freeze.
Ricardo says 2 weeks for this oil; the safety source is shorter, so we use 4 days.
Great British Chefs says 2 weeks for herb oil; the safety source is shorter, so we use 4 days.

preps.name: Coconut foam
preps.description: A light, sweet coconut cream foam from a siphon, for topping coffee drinks, tropical sours and highballs.

steps.body: Stir the cold milk, cream and coconut syrup together and pour into a 0.5 L siphon.
Screw on one N2O cream charger and shake the siphon 6 to 8 times. Stop once it dispenses thick; it won't need shaking again.
Keep it in the fridge. Hold it upside down to dispense onto the drink, and never open it while it is still under pressure.

sources.note: iSi Coconut Cloud Topping: 200 ml milk, 300 ml cream (min. 32% fat) and 50 ml coconut syrup in a 0.5 L whip with one charger, shaken 6 to 8 times. Used as written.

Second source (Room for Improvement via Punch) builds a coconut foam on a 14 oz can of coconut cream with 50 g sugar, 35 ml falernum, 3 g salt and 1 g Foam Magic, one N2O charge. A different style; we use iSi's ratio, the maker's own.
Ohio State University Extension storage chart: sweetened whipped cream keeps 1 day in the fridge. Applied as the general keep for this sweetened cream and milk foam.
iSi: cream left in a sealed, chilled whipper keeps up to 10 days. Applies to this cream foam only while sealed in the siphon; the shorter food-safety keep wins.

preps.name: Dashi
preps.description: Japanese stock of kombu and bonito flakes, clean and deeply savoury. For umami in savoury Martinis, Bloody Mary styles and broth drinks.

recipe.note: one 10 cm square, a few slits cut in it

steps.body: Optional: soak the kombu in the water for 2 to 3 hours (or up to 12 hours in the fridge) first.
Heat the kombu and water over medium-low until almost boiling, about 10 minutes, skimming. Lift out the kombu before it boils, or the dashi turns slimy and bitter.
Add the bonito flakes, bring back to the boil, simmer 30 seconds and turn off the heat.
Let the flakes settle for about 10 minutes, then strain through a fine sieve.

sources.note: Just One Cookbook awase dashi: 10 g kombu, 10 g katsuobushi, 4 cups water (960 ml at 240 ml a cup). Used as written.
One batch makes about 800 ml.
For this dashi: 3 to 5 days in the fridge, 2 weeks frozen. We use the short end, 3 days.

preps.name: Dill oil
preps.description: Blanched dill blended into neutral oil and dripped clear: a green, grassy oil for drops on savoury drinks and garnishes. Starting point: test a batch first.

keeps.storage: Fridge at 4 °C or below, sealed bottle

steps.body: Blanch the dill for 30 seconds, then straight into iced water.
Squeeze it dry and pat dry on a clean cloth.
Blend with the oil until the outside of the blender feels hot, then chill it fast in a bowl set over iced water.
Strain through a coffee filter overnight. Don't press.
Botulism risk: fresh herbs in oil must stay cold. Bottle, refrigerate straight away, label with the date, and throw it out after 4 days (or freeze it).

sources.note: Great British Chefs' herb oil for any soft herb: 200 g herbs to 300 g groundnut oil (1 : 1.5), blanched 30 seconds. The page doesn't name dill; it is a soft herb, so we apply the method untested.
NCHFP's rule for fresh garlic in oil, from its research on vegetables and herbs stored in oil: fridge at 4 °C or below, no more than 4 days, or freeze.
Great British Chefs says 2 weeks for herb oil; the safety source is shorter, so we use 4 days.

preps.name: Egg white foam
preps.description: A mousse-like siphon foam of egg white and a flavourful liquid such as fruit juice or cold tea, spooned or piped onto drinks.

recipe.note: pasteurised is the safe choice; about 2 whites
or cold tea; fine strained, not oily, any alcohol kept under 10%

steps.body: Raw egg: use pasteurised egg white. Whisk it into the cold juice or tea, sweeten with a little syrup if you like, and strain fine.
Pour into a 1 L siphon so it is no more than half full. Screw on one N2O cream charger and shake 6 times; over-shaking hurts it.
Chill the siphon at least 40 minutes before use. Never put it in the freezer.
Dispense upside down onto the drink. If it won't foam, shake and try again; never charge it more than twice. Keep it cold and bin it after 2 days.

sources.note: About one egg white (30 ml) per 200 ml flavourful liquid, siphon filled to half, one 8 g N2O cartridge per half litre, shaken six times, chilled 40 minutes. Scaled to 60 ml white and 400 ml liquid.
Second source: iSi's orange espuma allows 150 ml pasteurised egg white to 350 ml juice and tonic, a much richer white ratio. We use Difford's 1 white per 200 ml as the general base for any liquid.
Ohio State University Extension storage chart: raw egg whites keep 2 to 4 days in the fridge. We take the short end, 2 days.
Difford's: a cold egg white foam in a charged siphon lasts around a week. Longer than the food-safety keep for raw whites, so the 2 days above wins.

preps.name: Fermented chili
preps.description: Chopped fresh chillies salted at 3% by weight and left to ferment into a sour, hot mash. Blend or strain for hot sauce, brines and spicy margaritas.

steps.body: Wear gloves. Weigh the chopped chillies and mix in 3% salt by weight (30 g per kg).
Leave in the bowl for 15 to 30 minutes to draw out juice.
Pack tightly into a clean jar and weight it so everything stays under the liquid. Leave at room temperature.
Taste daily; refrigerate when it's sour enough. Throw it out if you see mould.

sources.note: Revolution Fermentation (a ferment culture maker) puts chili peppers at 3 to 4% salt by vegetable weight; its table gives 30 g per 1 kg at 3%. We use 3%, dry-salted, soaked 15 to 30 minutes, packed under a weight.

preps.name: House bitters
preps.description: Aromatic bitters made in house: gentian and mugwort for bite, orange peel and warm spice for aroma, rested two weeks in strong vodka. Dash into Old Fashioneds, Manhattans and anything that wants a bitter backbone.

steps.body: Put the raisins, dried peel, gentian, mugwort, cardamom, allspice and cloves in a 1 litre glass jar. Pour in the 50% ABV vodka, seal and shake.
Leave in a cool, dark place for 2 weeks, shaking every other day. With 40% ABV vodka, give it 3 weeks. High-proof spirit is flammable: keep it away from flames and burners.
Strain through a fine sieve lined with three layers of cheesecloth, pressing the solids to get all the liquid out. Discard the solids.
Return to a clean jar, add the simple syrup and shake gently. Bottle into dasher or dropper bottles and label with the name and date.

sources.note: ATK tested recipe, as written: 1/4 cup raisins (4 tbsp), 1/2 oz each dried orange peel and gentian chips (14 g), 2 tbsp mugwort, 8 cardamom, 10 allspice, 4 cloves in 16 oz 100-proof vodka (480 ml), 2 weeks, then 1 oz simple syrup (30 ml). 80 proof: add a week.
Recipe states it makes about 16 oz (480 ml).
Keep for this exact recipe: up to a year in a cool, dark place.

preps.name: House-pickled onion
preps.description: Thin-sliced onions under a hot vinegar brine, kept in the fridge: a Gibson garnish and a sharp brine for savoury drinks.

recipe.note: peeled and thinly sliced, enough to pack 2 pint (500 ml) jars tightly

keeps.storage: Fridge, lidded jars. Never shelf stable

steps.body: Peel, rinse and thinly slice the onions, and pack them tightly into clean jars.
Boil the vinegar, water, salt and sugar for 2 minutes.
Fill the jars to 1 cm below the rim, cover and refrigerate.
Give it a day or two before using. Use within 2 weeks.

sources.note: UC Master Food Preservers' pickled onions, per jar: 1 cup vinegar, 1 cup water, 1 tbsp pickling salt, 2 tsp sugar; onions to fill, as the brine ratio is what matters. Doubled for 2 jars.
For these pickled onions: use within 2 weeks.

preps.name: Lacto-fermented tomato
preps.description: Chopped tomatoes salted at 2% by weight and left to ferment sour under their own juice. For savoury, tangy brines in Bloody Marys and Martinis.

steps.body: Weigh the chopped tomatoes and mix in 2% salt by weight (20 g per kg).
Leave in the bowl for 15 to 30 minutes to draw out juice.
Pack tightly into a clean jar and weight it so everything stays under the liquid. Leave at room temperature.
Taste daily; refrigerate when it's sour enough. Throw it out if you see mould.

sources.note: Revolution Fermentation (a ferment culture maker) puts tomatoes at 2% salt, dry-salted by vegetable weight: 20 g per 1 kg, soaked 15 to 30 minutes then packed under a weight. Below 2% needs a starter culture.

preps.name: Leche De Tigre
preps.description: A drinkable leche de tigre from Lil' Deb's Oasis: orange and lime juice blended with fresh turmeric, ginger, jalapeño and garlic, then strained and salted. Bright, hot and savoury.

recipe.note: a 5 cm piece, peeled and thinly sliced

steps.body: Blend the orange juice, lime juice, turmeric, ginger, jalapeño and garlic until smooth.
Strain through a fine sieve and season with salt.
Cover and chill. Make it no more than a day ahead.

sources.note: Lil' Deb's Oasis (Hudson, NY) in Bon Appetit: 2 cups orange juice (480 ml), 1 cup lime juice (240 ml), a 3 inch piece turmeric, a 2 inch piece ginger, 1 jalapeño, 2 garlic cloves, salt to taste. Used as written.
Makes about 3 cups (720 ml).
For this recipe: can be made 1 day ahead, covered and chilled.

preps.name: Lemon curd
preps.description: A thick, sharp-sweet custard of lemon, sugar, eggs and butter, cooked to 77 °C. For lemon meringue style drinks, rims and garnishes.

recipe.note: bottled in the tested recipe, for steady acidity
unsalted, chilled, cut into 2 cm pieces

keeps.storage: Fridge, covered; or freeze up to a year

steps.body: Stir the sugar and zest together and leave for about 30 minutes.
In the top of a double boiler, off the heat, whisk the yolks and whole eggs, then whisk in the sugar and zest, the lemon juice and the butter.
Set over gently boiling water and stir constantly until it reaches 77 °C (170 °F) on a thermometer. This cooks the eggs safely.
Off the heat, keep stirring until it thickens, about 5 minutes. Strain out the zest.
Cool with wrap pressed onto the surface, then refrigerate, or freeze for longer storage.

sources.note: NCHFP tested curd: 2 1/2 cups superfine sugar (500 g at 200 g a cup), 1/2 cup zest (8 tbsp), 1 cup bottled lemon juice (240 ml), 3/4 cup butter (12 tbsp, 170 g), 7 yolks, 4 eggs, cooked to 170 °F. Second source runs about half the sugar; we use NCHFP.
King Arthur: 248 g sugar, 227 g lemon juice, 4 eggs plus 2 yolks, 113 g butter (8 tbsp), also to 170 °F. About 1 : 1 sugar to juice against NCHFP's 2 : 1; we use the tested NCHFP recipe.
The same NCHFP recipe makes 3 to 4 half-pint jars (720 to 960 ml); we give the lower figure.
For this recipe: frozen up to a year; once thawed in the fridge, use within 4 weeks.
King Arthur's lower-sugar curd (less preserved than ours) keeps 1 week in the fridge; we use this shorter keep.

preps.name: Meringue
preps.description: Swiss meringue: egg whites and sugar warmed to 80 °C over water, then whipped thick and glossy. For piping and torching on top of sours and lemon meringue style drinks.

keeps.storage: Fridge, covered or in a piping bag

steps.body: Whisk the whites, sugar and salt in a heatproof bowl over gently simmering water until the sugar dissolves and it reads 80 °C, about 8 minutes.
Take it off the heat and whip on medium until thick and glossy.
Spoon into a piping bag. Keep cold and use within 24 hours.

sources.note: Great British Chefs' Swiss meringue: 4 large egg whites, 200 g caster sugar, a pinch of salt, heated over water to 80 °C (about 8 minutes) then whipped. Used as written.
For this Swiss meringue: up to 24 hours in the fridge without weeping.

preps.name: Miso caramel
preps.description: Caramel syrup with red miso whisked through: savoury-sweet, less cloying than plain caramel. Made at Jyan Isaac Bread to sweeten a flat white; works in coffee and dark spirit drinks.

steps.body: Put the miso in a bowl and whisk in the caramel syrup a little at a time until fully emulsified and smooth.
Bottle and label.

sources.note: Megumi Ota Geronimo (Jyan Isaac Bread, Santa Monica): 1/2 oz caramel syrup to 1 tsp red miso, whisked until emulsified (15 ml : 5 ml, 3 : 1 by volume). Scaled 12 times: 180 ml and 12 tsp (4 tbsp).

preps.name: Orange foam
preps.description: A vegan orange espuma of orange juice and tonic lifted with a plant-based egg white, for coffee tonics and citrus highballs.

recipe.note: plant-based egg white; or 150 ml pasteurised egg white

steps.body: Pour everything into a 0.5 L siphon. Strain the juice fine first so pulp can't block the valve.
Screw on one N2O cream charger and shake hard 10 to 12 times.
Keep it cold until service and dispense upside down onto the drink. If you swap in egg white, use pasteurised.

sources.note: iSi vegan orange espuma: 0.5 tsp orange extract, 200 ml strained orange juice, 150 ml tonic and 150 ml plant-based egg white in a 0.5 L whip, one charger, 10 to 12 shakes. Used as written.

preps.name: Pandan cream
preps.description: A malty, grassy pandan whipped cream from a siphon, made with pandan syrup, for topping coffee and rum drinks or shots.

recipe.note: Punch's: 240 ml water, 200 g sugar, 1 pandan leaf

steps.body: For the syrup: boil the water, take it off the heat, add the pandan leaf so it is submerged, cover and leave 30 minutes.
Lift out the leaf and stir in the sugar until it dissolves. Cool.
Stir the cream, 120 ml of the syrup and the malt powder together until the malt dissolves.
Pour into a 0.5 L siphon, charge once with N2O, turn it upside down and shake 4 times. Keep it cold and use within a day.

sources.note: Malted pandan whipped cream (CrossFit Breakfast, Punch): 1 cup cream, 1/2 cup pandan syrup (1 cup water, 1 cup sugar, 1 pandan leaf steeped 30 min) and 1 1/4 tsp malt powder, charged once, shaken 4 times. Cups to ml at 240 ml, sugar cup at 200 g.
Ohio State University Extension storage chart: sweetened whipped cream keeps 1 day in the fridge. Applied as the general keep for this sweetened pandan whipped cream.

preps.name: Pickled cucumber
preps.description: Fridge pickles: cucumbers packed in jars under a boiled sour vinegar brine. A garnish, and the brine goes into dirty Martinis and pickleback-style shots.

recipe.note: washed and cut, enough to pack 4 pint (500 ml) jars snugly
white (or apple cider); never dilute it more than this

keeps.storage: Fridge, lidded jars. Never shelf stable

steps.body: Wash and cut the cucumbers; no cooking needed. Pack them snugly into clean jars, with up to 2 tbsp of herbs or spices per jar (dill, garlic, mustard seed, peppercorns) if you like.
Boil the vinegar, water, salt and sugar for 2 minutes.
Pour the brine over the cucumbers to 1 cm below the rim, lid the jars and refrigerate.
Let the flavour develop for 1 to 2 days before serving. Use within 2 weeks.

sources.note: UC Master Food Preservers' sour brine for quick fridge pickles (cucumbers named): 3 cups vinegar (720 ml), 3 cups water, 3 tbsp pickling salt, 2 tbsp sugar optional; boil 2 minutes; enough for up to 4 jars. Used as written.
For these refrigerator pickles: use within 2 weeks.

preps.name: Sobolo
preps.description: West African hibiscus drink, called sobolo in Ghana: dried hibiscus simmered with ginger, lemon and cinnamon, strained and sweetened. Tart and deep red, served chilled as a soft drink or a base for long drinks.

recipe.note: or sweetener of choice, to taste

steps.body: Rinse the dried hibiscus well in a colander to wash off grit.
Put the hibiscus, water, chopped ginger, lemon and cinnamon sticks in a pot and bring to the boil.
Turn down to a simmer for 15 to 20 minutes.
Strain through a fine sieve, then stir in the sweetener while it is still hot.
Cool and chill. It comes out strong: dilute with water to taste. For a Ghanaian-style spiced sobolo, cloves, black pepper and chilli are often added.

sources.note: 2 cups dried hibiscus, 1/2 lemon, 2 cinnamon sticks, 5 tbsp chopped ginger, 1/2 cup sweetener of choice, 10 cups water; simmer 15 to 20 min. Cups to ml at 240; 1/2 cup sugar taken as 100 g (the source uses monk fruit).
Makes 8 cups (1920 ml) before any dilution.
About a week in the fridge, for this same recipe made with a no-sugar sweetener (no more preserved than a sugar version).

preps.name: Strawberry foam
preps.description: A vegan strawberry espuma set with a little agar, for topping sours, spritzes and desserts.

steps.body: Blend everything smooth, then bring it to the boil in a pan and take it off the heat once it thickens.
Pour it through a fine sieve into a 0.5 L siphon. Screw on one N2O cream charger and shake hard 12 to 16 times.
Chill the siphon at least 4 hours so the agar sets.
Shake again before the first use, then dispense upside down.

sources.note: iSi vegan strawberry espuma: 50 ml vegan cream (31%), 100 ml water, 300 g strawberries, 2 g agar, 100 g icing sugar; boiled, sieved into a 0.5 L whip, one charger, 12 to 16 shakes, 4 hours cold. Used as written.

preps.name: Ube foam
preps.description: A purple sweet cream foam of cream, milk and ube condensed milk from a siphon, for iced coffee, chai and matcha drinks.

recipe.note: up to 100 g for a stronger flavour

steps.body: Stir the cream, milk and ube condensed milk together until smooth.
Pour into a 0.5 L siphon, screw on one N2O cream charger and shake hard 6 to 8 times.
Keep it in the fridge until service and dispense upside down onto the drink.

sources.note: iSi Ube Sweet Cream Cloud: 200 ml cream, 250 ml milk and 50 g ube condensed milk in a 0.5 L whip, one charger, 6 to 8 shakes. iSi says up to 100 g ube condensed milk for more flavour. Used as written.
Ohio State University Extension storage chart: sweetened whipped cream keeps 1 day in the fridge. Applied as the general keep for this sweetened cream and milk foam.
iSi: cream left in a sealed, chilled whipper keeps up to 10 days. Applies to this cream foam only while sealed in the siphon; the shorter food-safety keep wins.

preps.name: Whipped cream
preps.description: Lightly sweetened vanilla whipped cream from a siphon, for Irish coffee, flips and dessert drinks.

steps.body: Chill the cream and the siphon. Stir the sugar and vanilla into the cold cream until the sugar dissolves.
Pour into a 0.5 L siphon, no higher than its fill line. Screw on one N2O cream charger and shake 4 to 6 times.
Test a little: if it comes out runny, shake once more. Once it is right, don't shake it again or it turns cakey.
No siphon: whisk the cold cream by hand or mixer to soft peaks, add the sugar and vanilla, then whisk just to stiff peaks.
Keep it in the fridge and use within a day. It should not sit out more than 2 hours.

sources.note: Siphon whipped cream: 225 g heavy cream, 16 g superfine or icing sugar, 4 g vanilla extract, shaken 4 to 6 times after charging. Scaled x2 to 450 g cream to fill a 0.5 L siphon.
Second source: plain chilled double or whipping cream, 300 ml whipped to about 600 ml, with sugar or vanilla only to taste and no amount given. We use the AFME sweetened ratio.
Charger count: one cream charger for a 0.5 L whip, two for 1 L.
Ohio State University Extension storage chart: sweetened whipped cream keeps 1 day in the fridge. Applied as the general keep for sweetened whipped cream.
Iowa State University Extension: plain whipped cream is best served the day it is made, and no more than two hours at room temperature.
iSi: cream left in a sealed, chilled whipper keeps up to 10 days. Applies to whipped cream only while sealed in the siphon; the shorter food-safety keep wins.
